messages.author: 979e6ae871655730
messages.subject: How to change fonts/add custom fonts in ggplot2
parts:
Dear list,

Apologies for not having my question detailed in the content of this
email. Since it involves a list, a reasonably large table, and around
25 lines of code I thought it would be best if I included this link to
my post tonight on Stack Overflow: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/4094094/modifying-fonts-in-ggplot2

Summary of my problem: I need to change the standard helvetica default
in ggplot2 to a custom font type. Before I do this, however, I want to
be able to change the fonts in my graph to 'courier'. From there, my
(naive?) hope is that I will be able to update R's font library with
the custom font, and bring it in using the same call I used for
'courier.'

So two questions: (1) How do I change fonts in a ggplot? (I've looked
at several other posts on this, including on this list, and haven't
had any luck, yet), and (2) any thoughts about how to update R's font
library with a custom font?

Again, the data, code, and a list of resources I've already consulted
are found on the link above. I just wanted to bring this question to
the attention of this group.

Best wishes, and thanks in advance.
Aaron

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: How to change fonts/add custom fonts in ggplot2
parts:
Have a look at the family argument of theme_text()

dummy <- data.frame(A = rnorm(10), B = rnorm(10))
ggplot(dummy, aes(x = A, y = B)) + geom_point()
#helvetica = default
ggplot(dummy, aes(x = A, y = B)) + geom_point() + opts(axis.title.x
= theme_text(family = "sans", face = "bold"))
#times
ggplot(dummy, aes(x = A, y = B)) + geom_point() + opts(axis.title.x
= theme_text(family = "serif", face = "bold"))
#courier
ggplot(dummy, aes(x = A, y = B)) + geom_point() + opts(axis.title.x
= theme_text(family = "mono", face = "bold"))

HTH,

Thierry
